name: Thinking Logos
tagline: Bake an SVG into seven React agent-loading states, forked from thinking-orbs
description:
Thinking Logos turns an SVG into a dotted loading animation. The homepage meta description says it bakes any SVG into a dot cloud and plays it as seven agent loading states, with auto dark/light and no rasteriser at runtime. The README names the states thinking, solving, listening, searching, working, waiting, and generating.

The README says it is a fork of Jakub Antalik's thinking-orbs. The renderer and the orb states stay his, and ThinkingOrb is still exported. This fork adds a bake pipeline and seven logo states. Getting started says there is no package to install: open the playground, drop in an SVG, and copy the generated React file. The npm registry returned 404 for the name thinking-logos. A later README section imports bakeLogo from 'thinking-logos/bake' for a local bake. The LICENSE file is MIT, with copyright lines for Jakub Antalik on the engine and Enes Ozturk on the logo baking and logo modes.
agent_guidance:
Copy the React file the playground generates after you drop in an SVG. The README says that file already contains the baked points, and that nothing rasterises the SVG at runtime. Do not npm install thinking-logos. The registry returned 404 for that name on this check.

The license is MIT. The README says the orb engine is still Jakub Antalik's, and that ThinkingOrb remains a drop-in. Use a logo state when the loading mark should stay recognisable. The seven names are in the README.
why_it_matters: It is a checked way to turn a brand mark into an agent loading state without shipping a rasteriser.
tier_reason: MIT, a public playground, and a README that names the seven states and the fork. The GitHub API did not return a push date, and the package name in the bake example is not on npm.

description:

The part read here uses a Linear marketing animation for Product Intelligence, a button scale-down, Sonner's enter animation, and a morphing feedback control as examples. He writes that the morph is fine when people rarely see it, and that the same motion becomes irritating if they use it many times a day. A banner says enrollment for aiforui.dev is open with 7 days left. A reuse license was not on the page. His homepage is already a separate catalog record.
agent_guidance:
